evidence.source: CASE Press / National Taiwan University science communication
evidence.field: earliest secure attestation and graphic history
evidence.text: The article says 干 is securely attested by the mid-Western Zhou bronze inscription on 豦簋. It describes the sign as a round shield-like form with a forked top; later Western Zhou examples regularize the top to a short horizontal stroke, a form continued in later script traditions. The article presents the attribution of earlier Shang signs to 干 as a proposal and discusses the competing shield-decoration interpretation of their projecting points.
evidence.title: 商周時期的防護裝具與兵器：甲、冑、干、盾（四）

evidence.text: Commons describes this file as a vector tracing of the reverse inscription of oracle bone corpus item 甲骨文合集 10465, dated broadly to Late Shang, c. 1250–1050 BCE. The image is an uploader-made tracing, not a photograph of the artifact; the file page states CC0 1.0.

evidence.field: database query page and usage scope
evidence.text: The page identifies 小學堂 as an Academia Sinica character-form evolution database. The query page loaded, but its interactive fields did not return a rendered record for 干 in the web view. I therefore do not use a Xiaoxuetang image candidate here.

evidence.text: The file page describes 甲骨05.svg generally as oracle-bone-script characters and records an uploader public-domain dedication. The page does not identify which glyphs are shown or connect any one glyph to 干, so it is not selected as an image candidate.

search_audit.query: Wikimedia Commons 干 oracle bone script shield glyph file
search_audit.outcome: Search located an uploader-made oracle-bone tracing and a general oracle-bone script image. Opened both file-description pages; only the former has an identified source inscription and period, while neither page establishes that its pictured glyph is 干.

search_audit.query: site:commons.wikimedia.org 干 bronze script character shield
search_audit.outcome: Search returned the oracle-bone tracing. No specific, attributable bronze 干 glyph image with confirmed identity and reusable rights was established.

search_audit.query: 小學堂 干 字形 演變 CC0 干
search_audit.outcome: Opened the official evolution database and attempted a direct character query; the interface did not expose a rendered record or image in this web view. The system's rights page was not opened, and no Xiaoxuetang asset is proposed.
Opened and inspected the article's text describing secure mid-Western Zhou 豦簋 evidence, later graphic regularization, and the disputed identification of proposed Shang antecedents.

gaps: The Commons tracing is sourced to a Shang oracle-bone inscription, but the page does not label an individual sign as 干; its identity and relevance to this entry are not established, so no image is selected.
The general Commons oracle-bone graphic likewise lacks a character-level identification; despite its stated public-domain dedication, it is not selected.

The accessible Xiaoxuetang interface did not return a visible per-character record or direct glyph image. No official rights notice was verified during this search, so no Xiaoxuetang glyph is proposed.

A suitable glyph image with both a traceable original source and a page-grounded identification as 干 was not established. The article reports relevant script-history descriptions, but does not supply an independently licensed direct image candidate confirmed here. No images are returned.

limitations.text: No image candidate met the identity and provenance threshold. The researched paleographic source supports the script-history context, but the inspected image pages do not establish that their glyphs depict 干.
